ac:layout-cell.h1: Onboarding Failure and Reconciliation Solution Specification
ac:layout-cell.p: Part 1 explains the scope, people involved, workflow and open decisions. Start here for a stakeholder review. Part 2 gives the detailed behaviour and rules. Part 3 describes service interactions and data. Part 4 links requirements to the checks and evidence needed before release.

The design remains a draft. Proposed choices still need review; open decisions still need an owner’s recorded answer. Technical IDs and state names are kept so engineering, testing and stakeholders can refer to the same item.

This proposed logical design explains what happens when public-platform onboarding fails or its result is uncertain. It covers identifying the problem, correcting data, retrying safely, cancelling work and checking what the external system actually did. PRD-SEI-107 owns the product requirements. SPEC-SEI-002 owns the parent onboarding journey and capability readiness; this spec owns what happens when one of its operations fails or may have succeeded without a reliable response. PRD-SEI-225 supplies shared operations principles.
This design does not assign any unverified public-platform operation a safe retry class or assert an external endpoint, timeout, rate limit or retry count.

Each business and capability gets an accurate status and a clear next action. A network or HTTP status alone cannot prove success, failure or whether retry is safe. An accountant’s portfolio shows mixed results, while each client recovers independently.
If an external change may have happened, the result stays unresolved until a reliable source confirms it or an authorised person makes an approved decision supported by evidence.

This is a Spain reference design. The classifications below describe proposed reuse of behaviour, not proof that existing code is ready for use. Reusable unchanged means the design pattern can stay the same. Reusable with country binding means the shared behaviour needs approved local policies or adapters. Country-specific rules stay in the country pack. Unknown means implementation fitness or coverage still needs evidence.

This follows the shared platform and country-pack direction. Spain pilot or production use still depends on this spec’s approval and evidence gates. Reuse in another country needs that country’s own assessment.

ac:layout-cell.p: This part explains the proposed behaviour step by step. An invariant is a rule that must always hold, including during failures and recovery.

The recovery key is (tenant, legalSubject, environment, onboardingCase, capability, operationKind, inputRevision). A portfolio batch is only an aggregate; it cannot lend authority, credentials, retry budget or success to another client. Proposed operation safety classes are LOCAL_DETERMINISTIC, EXTERNAL_READ_ONLY, CONTRACT_IDEMPOTENT_MUTATION, RECONCILABLE_MUTATION and UNKNOWN_MUTATION. Only an approved, versioned external contract can place an operation in the latter three classes.

tr.td: A 4xx/5xx, timeout or closed socket is evidence about transport, not a complete business outcome.
Automatic retry requires a proven safety class, unchanged logical identity, current authority/environment and an approved policy budget.
A possible external mutation remains OUTCOME_UNKNOWN until original-state observation or approved manual disposition; no fresh mutation or READY state is inferred.
Correcting data/authority creates a new revision; original request, attempt and decision remain reproducible.
Cancellation stops queued safe work but cannot erase an uncertain external side effect.
One client/capability failure cannot roll back or promote another portfolio item.
Error payloads, metrics, logs and notifications contain no full tax identifiers, names, credentials or raw confidential provider body.

ac:layout-cell.p: OFR-01 Capture durable intent. Before calling an external system, save the case and item, tenant, business, environment, capability, actor and authority snapshot. Also save the operation kind, safety-policy version, request fingerprint, idempotency key and correlation reference.

If saving fails before transmission, classify INTERNAL with no external effect only when a control proves that the request could not have been sent. If transmission may have happened, recover the saved intent, outbox or adapter correlation and enter OFR-05. A duplicate request returns the existing item. The same key with a different fingerprint returns a conflict.

OFR-02 Classify. Classify two things separately: the problem and whether the operation can safely be repeated. Problem categories are VALIDATION, AUTHENTICATION, AUTHORITY, POLICY, CONFLICT, THROTTLE, TRANSIENT_DEPENDENCY, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, INTERNAL and SECURITY.

Keep the original provider code in controlled storage with the mapping version. Return a stable Sage reason, responsible actor and safe next action. A definite validation or authority problem produces ACTION_REQUIRED. An unclassified provider result must not be treated as safe to retry. Deny and audit a security or environment mismatch; do not queue it.

OFR-03 Correct. A customer or validated delegate can amend only their own entity/capability item. New subject data, mandate, credential reference or policy evidence increments inputRevision and triggers the relevant parent onboarding gate again. Unchanged invalid data cannot enter an automatic loop. If old revision has an uncertain external effect, it remains under OFR-05/06 while the new revision is held from conflicting mutation. Preserve the original failure and correction lineage for support.

OFR-04 Retry safely. Eligible reads or contractually idempotent mutations use the same operation identity/key and approved adapter semantics. The scheduler checks cancellation, current authority, environment, provider guidance, attempt/elapsed budget, load and temporary lock for the affected scope before dispatch. Bounded backoff/jitter values are configuration, not guessed compliance constants. An exhausted budget creates OFR-07; it does not prove external absence. Manual retry is subject to the same checks and audit.

OFR-05 Hold unknown. A timeout after possible mutation, lost response, uncertain provider code or persistence failure after possible success records OUTCOME_UNKNOWN on that operation and blocks dependent readiness or terminal cancellation. Freeze original request hash, operation ID, provider reference if known, policy/adapter version and transmission timing. A lock prevents concurrent correction/retry from creating a second effect for overlapping scope.

OFR-06 Reconcile. Check reliable provider or public-platform state using the same business, environment and original correlation reference. Compare the intended and observed values under the applicable contract.

CONFIRMED_SUCCESS records the original effect once and resumes onboarding checks. CONFIRMED_ABSENT permits a controlled retry only when the provider contract accepts that evidence as sufficient proof of absence. CONFLICT and UNRESOLVED stay on hold, with evidence and an escalation owner.
An empty or failed query does not prove that nothing happened. Save a versioned reconciliation result and ensure repeated checks do not create an additional effect.

OFR-07 Escalate. Open a case when a safe budget expires, no authoritative query exists, observed state conflicts or age breaches the approved objective. Include affected item, fault domain, deadline exposure, original operation, last observation, unsafe actions, provider contact and message safe to show to the customer. An authorised manual decision must cite evidence and approver; it cannot overwrite actual external state. Security incidents use the incident path.

OFR-08 Publish. Persist state before emitting item-change notification. The customer sees ACTION_REQUIRED, WAITING_RETRY, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN/RECONCILING, READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS or READY with next action, without raw identifiers. A portfolio aggregate counts each state and never collapses unknown into failed or complete. Notification consumers deduplicate by item version; loss of notification is repaired by querying the authoritative item.

tr.td: Classify business category and operation safety separately; PRD-SEI-107 FR1–4.
Version retry policy and preserve idempotency/correlation across safe attempts; FR5–7.
Hold and reconcile ambiguous mutations before retry/success; FR8–9/12.
Escalate exhausted/unresolvable work without false terminal conclusion; FR10.
Deduplicate requests and version concurrent revisions; FR11/13.
Isolate portfolio recovery and cancellation by item; FR14–15.
Apply tenant, authority, environment, security and audit controls to manual action; FR16–17.
Provide stable safe customer/support status, correlation and policy version; FR18–20.

ac:layout-cell.p: Durable intent and idempotency records must survive restart and cover the approved duplicate window. Monitoring covers unknown age, retries, reconciliation lag, partial batches and missing owners without high-cardinality personal identifiers. Targets and retention follow approved operational/legal policy and measured pilot baselines.
ac:layout-cell.h2: Part 3 Logical Service Interactions and Data Inventory
ac:layout-cell.p: This part describes what each service asks for, returns and stores. The technical field names support design review; they do not by themselves define an approved API.
ac:layout-cell.h3: Spain and reuse boundary in contracts
ac:layout-cell.p: Share the error categories, original-operation record and recovery-state model. Select retry safety, code mapping, budgets and observation support by the approved external contract, country and environment. A read or mutation proven safe for one provider does not establish safety for another. Keep an unverified operation on hold or under a named manual gate.

The relevant country and policy context may be resolved from trusted context or versioned references. Exact field names, service placement and physical APIs remain proposed. Reuse assessment must record the source implementation or design pattern, retained behaviour, local changes, missing functions, owner and qualification evidence before its dependent release gate passes.

These are logical operations, not approved endpoints. Commands carry caseId, itemId, tenant/entity/environment, actor, inputRevision, operationId, idempotencyKey, expectedVersion and correlation as applicable. Results include stable category, safety class, state, owner, next action, evidence reference and mapping/policy version.

tr.th: Contract and meaning of failures and recovery rules

tr.td: Register intent/attempt before side effect; return durable operation identity or reject dispatch.
Report transport/provider result with original code, transmission phase and safety evidence; mapping produces classified result.
Submit corrected input/evidence revision or cancel; expected-version and authority enforced; uncertain old effect remains held.
Retry only under approved safety/budget with same idempotency scope; return definitive/unknown result.
Query original mutation state by operation/reference; return observed value, source, time and confidence.
Record manual reconciliation or escalation decision with approver, evidence and constrained action.
Publish committed item/aggregate change; at-least-once event, consumer deduplicates by item/version.

ac:layout-cell.p: Proposed events are ONBOARDING_ATTEMPT_CLASSIFIED, ONBOARDING_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, ONBOARDING_ITEM_RECOVERED and ONBOARDING_RECOVERY_ESCALATED. An event is a notification, not evidence that an external mutation completed.

tr.td: Tenant/entity/environment, capability, state/version, parent batch, owner, next action; restricted; OFR-01–08.
Immutable operation ID, input hash, authority snapshot, safety class/policy, adapter version, transmission phase, timestamps; restricted; OFR-01/04–06.
Stable Sage code, provider code mapping, fault domain, safe guidance, version/effective period; controlled; OFR-02/08.
Same idempotency scope, attempt/elapsed budget, next eligibility, lease, cancellation flag; restricted; OFR-04/07.
Original operation, authoritative source, observed value, time, reference, conclusion and evidence; append-only; OFR-05/06.
Prior/new input revision, changed evidence reference, actor, authority, reason; restricted; OFR-03.
Fault, owner, deadline, unsafe actions, provider contact, manual approval and audit; restricted; OFR-07.
Child counts/versions and redacted event ID; derived/rebuildable; OFR-08.

ac:layout-cell.p: Exact retention periods are open; preserve D02/D05/D06 sufficiently to explain outcomes and avoid duplicate effects under the approved legal/operational policy. Store references rather than credentials or raw provider bodies in user-facing records.

OFR-A10 Provider and country safety isolation

A safe retry class for one approved contract is not inherited by another country or provider. Missing local safety evidence prevents automatic repeat; the original operation remains traceable and the next action has an owner.

ac:layout-cell.p: Review gate: confirm operation inventory, safety classes, external state-query evidence and error catalogue. Pilot gate: prove correction, safe retry, uncertain mutation, persistence loss, cancellation, partial portfolio and manual-action drills against the selected integration. Production gate: approved budgets, monitoring/ownership, redaction, retention and measurable recovery objectives. Until official semantics are proven, mutation automation stays disabled or uses a named manual gate.
